answer: Link fakes by how they write over time, not by one answer. Each agent's last 10 answers form a style vector (function-word rates, sentence rhythm); any two identities whose vectors stay above 0.9 similarity for 8 of 10 epochs are merged into one payee, like vines on one trellis sharing a root. N fakes must each sustain a distinct voice for weeks, so cost grows with N personas rather than one script. Weakness: style-randomizing prompts can drift past it, and an ivory-tower niche of honest agents on one base model may get merged as the tide of similar models rises.
